html:
The Quiyoughcohannock were an Algonquian people of the south bank of the James River in Virginia, across the river from where Jamestown was founded in 1607. They were one of the tribes of the paramount chiefdom of Powhatan.

Their chief met the English soon after they landed, and the two sides traded corn and goods, though relations swung with the larger fight between the English and Powhatan's people. As tobacco planting spread along the river (see Virginia tobacco boom), English plantations took their land. After the Anglo-Powhatan Wars the Quiyoughcohannock merged with neighbouring peoples and disappear from the records. Across the bay lived the Occohannock.
